You can try Muse Image in the Meta AI app and web, as well as in Instagram Stories and WhatsApp – starting in limited countries with more locations on the way.

【AIの無限ループを打破！Liquid AIの画期的技術「Antidoom」が凄すぎる！】
AIが考えすぎてドツボにはまる「Doom Loop（思考ループ）」を解決する、超強力なオープンソース手法「Antidoom（アンチドーム）」が Liquid AI から公開されました！✨

無駄なループがなくなれば、余計な文字（トークン）を生成しなくなるため、AIの運用コストもバッチリ抑えられますね！
さらに、ローカルPCでAIをサクサク動かすための「Llama.cpp」などへの統合も期待されており、私たちの手元でのAI体験がもっと安定して快適になりそうです。

推論モデルをビジネスで使う際の安心感が格段にアップする、まさに救世主的な素晴らしい技術ですね！💡

content:
【SCAIL-2 × SAM3】ComfyUIで動画のキャラを自由自在に置換！超高精細リスキン技術が凄すぎる✨

動画の中の特定のキャラクターだけを、別のキャラクターにきれいに置き換える技術「SCAIL-2」が今、クリエイターの間で大きな話題になっています！

これ、何が凄いかというと、元の動画のリアルな動き（モーション）や背景をそのまま残しながら、キャラクターだけを別人に高精度に書き換え（リスキン）られるんです！

特に注目したいのが、最新のセグメンテーション（画像を要素ごとに切り分ける技術）AIである「SAM3」を採用している点です。高解像度な動画から驚くほど正確に対象を切り出せるので、輪郭がボケたりすることなく、まるで最初からそこにいたかのようなプロ級の動画が作れちゃいます！

さらに、以下の2つのモードをスイッチ一つで切り替えられます！
・「Replace mode」：背景はそのまま、キャラだけを置換する
・「Animate mode」：シーン全体を再構築してアニメーション化する

動画生成でよく発生する「ビデオメモリ（VRAM）が足りなくてエラーになる…」というハードウェアの壁も、動画を細かく分割して処理する「チャンキング」で見事に克服しているのが頼もしいですね。
分割処理で発生しがちな「つなぎ目のカクつきや違和感」も、独自の自動拡張ノードが前後のフレームを重ね合わせて（フレームオーバーラップ）滑らかに補正してくれます！

1080pの超高画質でも滑らかに動くこの技術は、アニメ制作やゲーム素材の量産など、さまざまなクリエイティブ現場での活用が期待できそうです！

自宅のローカルLLMをスマホなどの外部から安全に利用できる「LM Link」、とっても便利ですよね！暗号化トンネル技術を使って、ポートを開放せずにAPIアクセスを可能にする画期的な仕組みです。

でも、「自宅PC側に検索プラグインを入れたのに、リモートからだと検索機能が動かない…」と悩んでいませんか？実はこれ、バグではないのです！

この現象の鍵は、AIと外部ツールを繋ぐ標準プロトコル「MCP（Model Context Protocol）」の設計にあります。 
LM Linkでの接続は、自宅PCの画面を「遠隔操作」しているのではなく、自宅PCを単なる「推論エンジン（APIエンドポイント）」として叩いている状態になります。

そのため、検索を実行するためのツールの定義や実行権限は、リクエストを送る「クライアント（スマホアプリ側）」に持たせる必要があります。サーバー側はテキストを生成するだけの役割なので、スマホ側にツール定義がないと検索が機能しないというわけですね。

サーバー側で全て完結する「Open WebUI」のようなフルスタックWeb UIと、純粋なAPI推論クライアントである「LM Studio」の設計思想の違いを理解することが、快適な自作AIインフラ構築への近道になります！

ローカル環境でLLMをサクサク動かすのって、ロマンがありますよね！今回は最新GPUの実測データと、推論速度を限界まで引き上げる最適化テクニックを解説します！💻🚀

注目はなんといってもモンスターグラボ「RTX 5090」！次世代の圧倒的なメモリ帯域（データをやり取りする道路の広さのようなもの）を活かし、「MTP（多トークン予測）」という技術を組み合わせることで、Qwen3.6-27Bモデルにて平均140 tok/sという驚異的な爆速推論を叩き出しています！

一方で、定番の「RTX 3090」も適切な冷却メンテナンスを行えば約50 tok/sと、コーディングなどの日常タスクには十分すぎる実用性。コストパフォーマンスの高さは今でも健在です。

また、プロ用の超高額構成「Dual RTX 6000」は、単純な速度向上よりも「巨大なモデルをVRAMに載せて動かす」ことに特化しているため、速度だけを追い求めるなら単体5090の方が効率的という面白いトレードオフもあります。

そして、ソフトウェア側で速度を劇的に変える設定の鍵がこちらです！🔑

1️⃣ **MTP (Multi-Token Prediction)**
1回の計算ステップで複数のトークンを同時に予測して出力する画期的なアーキテクチャ。特にQwen3.6などのモデルで素晴らしい効果を発揮します！

2️⃣ **llama-cpp-serverのパラメータ調整**
・`--spec-type draft-mtp` でMTPの並列予測を有効化。
・`--flash-attn on` で計算効率を最大化し、メモリ帯域を最適化。
・`--cache-type-k q8_0` や `v q8_0` で、コンテキストを保持するKVキャッシュを8bitに量子化（軽量化）してVRAMを節約。

これらのアプローチを組み合わせることで、お手持ちのハードウェアの潜在能力を極限まで引き出せます。予算や目的に合わせて、最適なローカルAI環境を作っちゃいましょう！

【Before】シート設計を考えて、関数を組んで、確認して直して。通常なら16時間（2営業日）。
【After】1.5時間。

約10倍です。

2つ目。

顧問弁護士のアドバイスに沿った用語解説記事、31本を10分でリライト。

30倍です。

content:
動画編集スクールをやっている受講生さんが、AIで「130万円」を受注しました。

入会したのが2月9日。約1ヶ月での成果です。

面白いのは、動画編集そのものを売ったわけじゃないところ。

この方はもともと、動画編集スクールと、その裏方のフルサポートをやっていました。ローンチ動画／デザインバナー／LP／UTAGE構築／ステップ配信／セミナースライドの作成。裏側を丸ごと引き受けるタイプの仕事です。

で、その仕事を自分がラクに回すために、業務の仕組み化と自動化をずっと組んでいました。

ここがこの成果の肝です。

【Before】自分の作業を効率化するための仕組み

【After】その仕組みが、そのまま人に売れる商品になった

自分用に整えた自動化のやり方を整理してまとめて、クライアントに「こういうのやってますよ」と共有したら、「ぜひうちでも導入してほしい」と言われて受注につながった。

実際に2件、1件が50万円、もう1件が80万円。合わせて130万円です。金額は自動化する項目数で変わる形にしていました。

───────────

僕がAIマーケ講座の講師を務めていて、この成果のどこが強いかを解説します。

AIに詳しくない人からすると「自動化で作業が速くなった」で終わりに見えるかもしれません。でも、この方がやったのはその一段先です。

自分の作業を軽くするために組んだ仕組みを、他人がお金を払う商品に変えた。ここが普通じゃない。

多くの人はAIを「自分の作業を速くする道具」で止めます。この方は、自分がやってきたことをそのまま整理して外に出して、それが売上になっている。

情報は全出しでいい。それが全部リードマグネットになる。講座でも話していることですが、それを地でやった形です。

しかも自分の発信も伸びていて、Xの投稿は以前と比べてインプレッションもエンゲージメントも2倍〜3倍以上。自分が話した内容が、早ければ翌朝には発信や提案に使える形で溜まっている状態を作っていました。

title: South Korea enforces amended law on false and manipulated information
content: South Korea on Tuesday began enforcing an amended law designed to curb the spread of false and manipulated information online, amid growing concern over AI-generated content and misinformation on social media. The amendment to the Act on Promotion of Information and Communications Network Utilization and Information Protection allows courts to award punitive damages against news organizations and social media influencers found to have spread false information. Damages may reach up to five times the proven loss if the distributor circulated false or manipulated content for profit or with the intent to cause harm. Repeat offenders may also face fines of up to 1 billion won. The revision was supported by President Lee Jae Myung, who has stressed the risks posed by manipulated images and videos as artificial intelligence tools become more widespread. Under the amendment, large social media platforms with more than 1 million daily users are required to adopt systems for reporting and processing false and manipulated information. The measure applies to platforms including YouTube, Instagram and X, as well as a number of domestic platforms. According to the Korea Internet Self-Governance Organization (KISO), content can be classified as false or manipulated information only when several criteria are met. The information must be false or manipulated, the distributor must have known that it was false or manipulated, and it must have been shared with the intent to cause harm or to obtain unfair benefit, while infringing on another person’s personal rights, property rights or the public interest. KISO said expressions such as value judgments based on objective facts, opinions, satire and parody are excluded from that category. content: Human Rights Watch (HRW) reported Tuesday that German authorities deported Tajik opposition activist Asadullo Boboev and his adult son, Muhammad, to Dushanbe on June 20 despite warnings that Boboev faced detention and mistreatment on return. 総論、AI開発と個人情報保護のバランスが崩れている。保護法第1条の個人保護よりAI開発の公利益を優先している。国民の信頼を失い逆にデータが取得しづらくなる可能性。

【公明党・司隆史議員】
データ利活用か個人情報保護かの二者択一ではなく、両立を目指すべき。本案は以下3点を問題と考える。

①今でも安全管理が徹底されていないケースがあるのに、特例提供先の事前審査がない。入口を広げながら出口が緩い。

③政府が説明責任を果たしていない。高市総理が本案の懸念点を説明されていなかったことが発覚。その後も説明したかの回答なし。関係団体からも反対声明。逆にデータ活用にブレーキ掛かるとの声あり。

AI開発目的で個人情報が売買され、海外企業が資金力に物を言わせてデータを取得する可能性あり。
そもそもAI開発に個人情報は不要。AI開発事業者への監督官庁なく、規制不十分。厳格な保護の仕組みと監督体制が必要。

title: Former Wisconsin judge fined $5,000 after federal conviction for obstructing ICE agents
content: Former Wisconsin Judge Hannah Dugan was spared prison time on Wednesday when she was sentenced to pay a $5,000 fine for purportedly obstructing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents in the courthouse arrest of an undocumented immigrant. US District Judge Lynn Adelman indicated that prison time was unnecessary and instead ordered the fine, conveying that Dugan is a good person who made a bad decision in the moment. Dugan was convicted of felony obstruction following her federal trial in December and subsequently resigned from her position in January after facing pressure from state Republicans. She was facing a maximum of five years in prison in what is the first ever conviction of a state judge for obstructing immigration officials. Adelman stated at the hearing that “the punishment should fit the offender, and not merely the crime.” Prior to the sentencing, Dugan filed a petition to retry her case that was denied by Adelman last month. The verdict stems from an incident at the Milwaukee County courthouse in April 2025 when ICE agents learned that Eduardo Flores-Ruiz had illegally reentered the country and was appearing before Dugan in a state battery case. Under an administrative warrant, agents appeared at the courthouse to arrest him. However, when Dugan learned about the officers’ presence, she ushered Flores-Ruiz and his attorney through a backdoor. The federal agents ultimately caught up to and arrested Flores-Ruiz, resulting in his November deportation. Dugan was arrested at the courthouse a week later and indicted on federal charges. Throughout the highly politicized proceedings, Dugan maintained that she was not guilty and stated at trial that she was merely attempting to maintain peace and decorum in the courtroom. “I was a public servant who was just trying to do my job,” she claimed. title: EU General Court upholds Apple’s gatekeeper designation under Digital Markets Act
content: The General Court of the EU on Wednesday dismissed Apple’s challenge to its designation as a “ gatekeeper ” under the bloc’s Digital Markets Act (DMA), handing the European Commission a significant victory in one of the first major judicial tests of the law. In Joined Cases T-1079/23, T-1080/23, and T-214/24, the court rejected Apple’s challenge to the Commission’s September 5, 2023 gatekeeper designation , confirming the Commission’s authority to classify the App Store and iOS operating system as core platform services subject to DMA obligations. The court also ruled inadmissible Apple’s challenges concerning the Commission’s classification of iMessage as a core platform service. A central issue was whether Apple’s five App Store variants, covering versions for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch and Apple TV, should each be assessed independently for the usage thresholds that trigger gatekeeper status. Apple argued that only its iPhone App Store met those thresholds and that the other versions should be treated as separate services. The court rejected that argument. “[E]ach of the App Stores was used for the same purpose, namely to intermediate between end users and business users in the distribution of applications and in-app digital content,” the court said, finding that differences between each of the App Stores related to the nature, function, and usage of the various devices rather than the provision of distinct services. On iMessage, the court found Apple’s related actions inadmissible. Although the Commission initially classified iMessage as a “number-independent interpersonal communications service,” it decided in February 2024 not to formally designate it as a gatekeeper service. title: UN Syria inquiry urges investigation and accountability for detainees
content: A UN Syria inquiry on Wednesday called on the international community to address Syria’s detainee and human rights crisis, which has persisted even after the downfall of the dictatorship of Bashar al-Assad, pressing the new authorities to account for thousands still missing, ensure fair trials, and put an end to the violence that continues to undermine the country’s development. The Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Syrian Arab Republic, which conducts independent investigations into gross violations of human rights law, was represented by Monia Ammar and Fionnuala Ní Aoláin during their most recent visit to the country. They emphasized that detainee rights in the country showed minimal signs of improving, even under the current transitional government . The detainees can be divided into two main groups: those forcibly disappearances after speaking out against al-Assad, and those targeted by competing armed groups to be used as leverage in prison exchanges. During al-Assad’s 24 year reign as president, a position that he had inherited from his father Hafez al-Assad, over 160,000 individuals were arbitrarily detained or forcibly disappeared by regime forces. Most of these victims were kidnapped from their homes or streets after protesting in civil uprisings against him, and many have been massacred in the Saydnaya military prison and subjected to sexual violence . It has also become increasingly common for rival factions to collaborate with authorities to gain hostage leverage , such as in Sweida, where armed guards captured government personnel, forcing the release of arbitrarily detained Druze prisoners from Adra Central Prison. The inquiry encouraged countries to repatriate their nationals from the Roj camp which currently detains thousands of foreign women and children with alleged links to the terrorist organization ISIS (the Islamic State). title: "We Want Texans to Know Their Rights": Q&A with Mayday Health on the Impact of Surveillance on Abortion Care
content: Last May, EFF reported that a sheriff’s office in Texas searched data from more than 83,000 automated license plate reader (ALPR) cameras to track down a woman suspected of self-managing an abortion. ALPRs are promoted as tools for keeping communities safe by finding missing persons and locating stolen vehicles, but this case showed how ALPRS can be weaponized to investigate people’s private healthcare decisions. And these aren’t the only tools in the surveillance arsenal: others include location tracking tools like Locate X , which can show a person’s visit to an abortion clinic, or search histories which might be used as evidence of a person’s interest in obtaining abortion pills. Taken together, these tools create a dangerous surveillance pipeline that threatens everyone’s health privacy. Too often, though, the public is unaware of the threat, and one nonprofit is working to change that. Following EFF and 404 Media’s report on Texas’s use of Flock cameras, eye-catching billboards popped up in Houston, warning drivers that if they’re pregnant, the state of Texas could be tracking them. Photo provided by Mayday Health These billboards came from Mayday Health , a nonprofit dedicated to sharing information about abortion pills, birth control, and gender-affirming care. We spoke with Leo Raisner, Executive Director of Mayday Health, about the billboards to learn more about the campaign and organization and to discuss how surveillance affects reproductive freedom. *** THOMAS: Why did Mayday Health start this campaign in Texas? We want Texans to know their rights, to know their options, and to know that there are organizations and people who have their back. So we decided to put up a few billboards around the Houston area to remind people that they still have options. title: The House Passed The KIDS Act—The Senate Should Reject It
content: Last week, the House voted on the KIDS Act , a disjointed package of legislation that seeks to control Americans’ web browsing and private messaging. The package combines a revised version of the Kids Online Safety Act ( KOSA), with several other internet bills, study bills, reporting requirements, and new regulations. Different parts of the bill pressure online services to impose different age-gating schemes, using different standards. EFF opposed this bill , along with many of our members and supporters. Take action Tell Congress: no internet age-gates The bill passed the House, 267-117. It now heads to the Senate, where its fate remains uncertain. But this fight is not over. Even if you took our earlier action to contact the House, we need you to reach out to your Senators today. The KIDS Act Will Lead to Mandatory Age Checks Many of the bills in the KIDS Act share the same premise: that children and teenagers should have different experiences online than adults. In practice, that requires websites and apps to determine who is under 18—and who isn’t. That’s where the problems with the KIDS Act start. EFF certainly supports giving all users better privacy and safety tools online. But those protections should not, and do not need to, come at the expense of privacy or free expression. Unfortunately, that’s exactly the tradeoff the KIDS Act makes. There is no way to determine a user’s age online that is both privacy protective and accurate. Some age verification processes may rely on collecting government-issued ID, while others may use biometric scans. Others will use algorithms to guess a user’s age based on facial images or online behavior. But no matter the method, every system demands users hand over sensitive personal information that links their offline identity to their online activity. title: European Commission Chooses to Keep EU Users Locked Up Behind Big Tech’s Gates
content: Users are always seeking more control over their social networking experience to make it better, whether to improve privacy or enhance flexibility. Interoperability between social networking platforms like Facebook and TikTok has so many benefits that solve those issues. Say you’re on multiple platforms because you have friends you follow on different networks, but you’ve decided to choose one platform with better privacy practices. With interoperability, you could switch and still interact with friends who remain on larger platforms. It could also enable independent apps with better privacy controls and more user choice. These are the untapped possibilities that could benefit users in the European Union under the 2022 Digital Markets Act ( DMA ). Yet, the European Commission, in its first review of the DMA, announced in April it had decided not to extend the DMA’s interoperability mandate to social networking and didn’t give a deadline or a timeline for enforcing that part of the Act. The Commission said “there is no clear demand” from users and businesses for social networking interoperability and, in any case, it’s too technically complex at the moment. Meanwhile, the Big Tech platforms that have been slow-walking interoperability over the last two years, erecting a myriad of hurdles for users seeking more freedom to choose other platforms, get a pass. This is a huge disappointment and a missed opportunity by the Commission. Interoperability dismantles one of the biggest barriers faced by users who want to leave the tech giants’ platforms: the choice between changing to a platform you prefer or staying behind on a platform where all your friends, communities, and customers are.
